newsitem.title: USA: Santander cuts Argentina, Brazil stock views.
newsitem.headline: Santander cuts Argentina, Brazil stock views.

text.p: Santander Investment said Wednesday it downgraded its long-term view on Argentina and Brazil and upgraded Venezuela in a reshuffling of its recommended Latin America equities portfolio.
The firm cut its 12-month view on Argentina to underweight from overweight, cutting its allocation to 9.5 percent from 11.5 percent.
"In our view, the market is unlikely to rebound convincingly as long as concerns over 1997 gross domestic product growth persist," Santander said.
It added that it also downgraded its long-term view on Brazil to underweight from market weight, reducing its weighting to 41.5 percent from 43 percent.
The firm said it expects structural reforms, fiscal deficit and the high real rate scenario to pressure the market after October's municipal elections in Brazil.
Elsewhere, Santander upgraded its 12-month view on Venezuela to overweight from underweight, boosting its allocation there to 3.5 percent from 1.5 percent.

"Economic stabilization measures should bear fruit in coming months, and the commitment to privatization -- despite the initial hiccup -- reinforces the credibility of efforts to steer the economy toward a stable platform for growth," the firm said.
Santander also added to its overweight position in Mexico, increasing it to 29 percent from 28.5 percent.
Regarding Chile, the firm increased its underweight allocation there to seven percent from six percent.
Santander kept its overweight positions in Colombia and Peru at 5.0 percent and 4.5 percent, respectively.
